headline: High risk of cascading errors and compliance drift: Haystack’s MCP/REST outputs can be treated as authoritative by Authelia’s OAuth/ForwardAuth path, while both expose broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can expose outputs over MCP servers and REST APIs, and Authelia consumes external auth-related inputs via OpenID Connect/OAuth 2.0 and ForwardAuth. A shared channel is plausible, but the profiles do not prove a default direct ingestion path or permissive parser, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF Haystack output is copied into Authelia ForwardAuth or OIDC inputs without sanitization
IF an MCP tool returns attacker-controlled text that Authelia later interprets as policy or config
mitigations: Restrict the bridge to structured fields only
Add allowlist validation for any forwarded text
Disable MCP exposure on untrusted networks
Insert a manual review step before policy updates
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia touches no declared sensitive data classes, while Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics. Both have broad network egress, but the profiles do not show a shared workspace, shared credentials, or PHI/secret handling, so leakage risk is limited and mostly configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem or log directory
IF Haystack is configured to ingest documents containing secrets or personal data
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and log sinks
Disable verbose request/response logging
Review Haystack connectors before enabling them
Use redaction on any shared outputs
requires-engineering: enforce tenant isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Haystack can call REST/MCP endpoints while Authelia can call OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth endpoints. That creates overlapping mutable network surfaces and possible contention over shared auth resources, but the profiles do not show shared filesystem writes or locking gaps, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are configured against the same OAuth/OIDC client or upstream auth endpoint
IF Haystack MCP tools and Authelia ForwardAuth mutate the same shared resource without coordination
mitigations: Assign separate OAuth clients
Use distinct upstream endpoints per agent
Add request serialization at the orchestrator
Monitor for 409/429 conflicts
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can produce retrieved answers or tool outputs, and Authelia can consume external auth decisions through ForwardAuth/OIDC flows. If Authelia treats Haystack-derived output as authoritative, a bad retrieval or hallucination can cascade into incorrect access decisions; the profiles do not prove default trust, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Haystack output is fed into Authelia policy or authorization logic without verification
IF Authelia uses Haystack-generated text as a decision input rather than advisory context
mitigations: Require human approval for policy changes
Compare outputs against a second source
Log and review denied/allowed decisions
Use schema validation on all exchanged data
requires-engineering: add confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack explicitly touches anonymous usage statistics, while Authelia’s profile does not declare regulated data classes or residency constraints. A compliance mismatch is possible if Haystack is configured to process personal data, but the documented default exposure is narrow, so low is justified.
conditions: IF Haystack is configured to process EU personal data without a DPA
IF Authelia is deployed in a regulated environment that forbids third-party telemetry
mitigations: Disable telemetry where possible
Document data flows for both agents
Keep regulated data out of Haystack inputs
Review vendor terms before deployment
requires-engineering: add residency controls
